liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **It's All Over Now Baby Blue** (1 review): The performance of this song is considered really well done by the listener [8]

## The recordings

- **gd66-09-16.sbd.vernon.9127.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 9 songs; 69 min; rated 4.76/5 by 17 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound quality is described as quite good, though not perfect, for this 1966 recording; Jerry Garcia is prominent in the mix, while drums are slightly less prominent; The 1966 recording has a distinct old rock and roll and bluesy sound [7][8][16][17]
- **gd1966-09-16.vintagedead.25283.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 9 songs; 69 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd66-09-16.sbd.tzuriel.11503.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 9 songs; 69 min; rated 5/5 by 5 [2]
- **gd1966-09-16.sbd.davenport.95970.flac16**: soundboard; 9 songs; 68 min; rated 3.71/5 by 7 [4]

## Around the show

- Stanley Mouse created a famous skeleton covered in roses poster to advertise this show [11]
- The poster's central image was lifted from Edmund J. Sullivan's 1859 Rubaiyat illustrations [12]
- Oxford Circle is listed as another artist performing at this event [5]
- The concert took place at the Avalon Ballroom in San Francisco, California [22]
- The date is likely inaccurate; the show is probably a composite of at least two shows [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd66-09-16.sbd.vernon.9127.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Raoul Duke and Matt Vernon; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: The albums were released against the band's will due to an MGM/Sunflower contract; The recording lineage is SBD to MR to CDR, seeded by Matt Vernon [1][14]
- **gd1966-09-16.vintagedead.25283.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by unknown; source: SBD>MR>??>CDR [3]. Also: The show appeared on "Vintage Dead" (1970) and "Historic Dead" (1971) on Sunflower Records [3]
- **gd66-09-16.sbd.tzuriel.11503.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Tzuriel; source: SBD ->? [2]
- **gd1966-09-16.sbd.davenport.95970.flac16**: transferred by Davenport; source: SBD>MR>?>LP [4]
